questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Complex Conjugate of a Complex Number With Positive Imaginary Part
questions.problem: What is the complex conjugate of $z=2+8\text{i}?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate, we flip the sign of the imaginary part.

In the given number $z=2+8\text{i},$ the imaginary part is $8\text{i}.$ Flipping the sign, we get $-8\text{i}.$

Therefore, the complex conjugate is given by $\overset{―}{z}=2-8\text{i}.$

What is the complex conjugate of $z=-\frac{1}{2}i?$ Use $i$ to denote the imaginary unit.

$\overset{―}{z}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate, we flip the sign of the imaginary part.

In the given number $z=-\frac{1}{2}i,$ the imaginary part is $-\frac{1}{2}i$ (there is no real part, just an imaginary part). Flipping the sign, we get $\frac{1}{2}i.$

Therefore, the complex conjugate is given by $\overset{―}{z}=\frac{1}{2}i.$
